title: Publishing, selling, sequencing, and indexing glass: a stricter taxonomy of microscope-slide forms
research_problem: Recent Cole, Elcock, Harvard and archive runs make it possible to separate several forms that all look superficially like 'numbered slide series' but perform different work. The central distinction is whether a material address organizes public replication/distribution, anatomical succession, commercial comparison, or later reference retrieval.
strict_publication_test: There is an explicit issue/set/series/catalogue architecture available beyond one private holder.
More than one recipient can in principle obtain a material unit under the same public address or product identity.
The address is part of distribution, not merely a later museum accession or private cabinet coordinate.
If physical copies vary, contemporary actors still treat them as equivalents within the issue/set/product system.

forms.case: Arthur C. Cole, Studies in Microscopical Science
forms.replication: subscriber preparations are equivalent publication units despite acknowledged biological non-identity
forms.retrieval: paper issue and numbered glass cabinet cross-reference one another after binding
forms.distinctive_mechanism: serial time organizes attention and distribution

forms.form: replicated numbered published collection / exsiccata-like set
forms.publication_status: yes when repository documentation establishes replicated published sets
forms.replication: same set number can occur in geographically separate replicate collections
forms.distinctive_mechanism: portable numbering stabilizes a distributed set without periodical cadence

forms.publication_status: commercial distributed knowledge object; use 'material publication' only if accompanying catalogue/set architecture is directly verified
forms.unit: one slide containing many named forms, e.g. advertised fifty-species Foraminifera Type Slides
forms.address: Type Slide number/category + numbered/spatial internal matrix
forms.replication: multiple sale copies implied by product advertising and distributed survival; exact copy-equivalence remains to be collated
forms.retrieval: species names/matrix on glass; contemporary review reportedly adds a printed catalogue/key, awaiting direct BHL verification
forms.distinctive_mechanism: classification is spatialized and compressed into one purchasable field of comparison
forms.grade: S for commercial Type Slide form; A+ for printed-key architecture until direct review transcription

forms.case: Norman, Bourgogne, Wheeler, Watson and related trade lists
forms.publication_status: catalogue is publication; each purchased preparation is not automatically an edition copy
forms.replication: multiple examples may be prepared, but stable physical equivalence cannot be assumed
forms.retrieval: surviving labels may preserve catalogue wording, maker marks, retailer labels and collector numbers
forms.distinctive_mechanism: stock and orderability rather than serial/set replication
forms.grade: S for catalogue system; object matching item-specific

forms.case: Harvard Embryological Collection / Minot and Balfour serial sections
forms.unit: successive physical sections from one embryo/specimen
forms.replication: parts are successive anatomical slices, not copies distributed under one public address
forms.retrieval: card catalogue, drawings, old/new identifiers, technique and publication links

forms.form: indexed research reference Type Slide archive
forms.publication_status: research reference collection; individual TS slides may underlie publications but the archive itself should not be called a material publication without distribution evidence
forms.unit: faunal association Type Slide, some with up to many species
forms.replication: primarily one curated reference archive, not demonstrated replicated distribution
forms.retrieval: loose-leaf Keys + card index + internal slide numbering
forms.distinctive_mechanism: cumulative research taxonomy and publication reference rather than commercial issue cadence
forms.historical_connection: some earliest slides are marked Charles Elcock, Belfast; Elcock mounting practice is recorded in the collection history

forms.replication: distributed-set logic is probable but exact editions/replicates require collation
forms.retrieval: catalogue/provenance tables and museum inventory are the target crosswalks
forms.grade: A+ pending La Plata series inventory and publication collation

forms.case: Haeckel correspondence, club exchange and direct donations
forms.unit: one object or bounded collection sent between named parties

decisive_comparisons.result: Both use seriality, but Cole's sequence is distributive/publication time and Minot's is anatomical continuity.
Cole distributes attention through time; Elcock compresses comparative attention into one spatial matrix.

Both use Type Slide language/form and indexed specimen fields, but one is documented as a commercial product while the later archive is a cumulative research reference system. Connection does not erase the difference in distribution model.
A catalogue makes an object orderable but does not by itself make every resulting slide a stable edition copy.

research_payoff: The project can now discuss material publication without inflating every numbered or circulating preparation into 'publication'. This makes Cole more distinctive, Elcock more precise, and Tempère–Peragallo a testable open category rather than a foregone comparison.
